subject: evs
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF
note: Listed by NCERT under the subject "The World Around Us". Hindi edition: Hamara Adbhut Sansar.

topics.title: Families and how they care for each other
outcomes: Learner can describe members of their family, how they help one another and how families can be different
misconceptions: Thinks every family looks like their own (same size, same members)
hooks: Who cooks, who fetches milk, who tells stories at night in your home?

topics.title: Friends, pets and playing together
outcomes: Learner can talk about friendships with people and animals and ways of caring for them
misconceptions: Believes pets do not have feelings
hooks: Bela and her dog: feeding street dogs safely

topics.title: What happens at a mela
outcomes: Learner can describe the people, stalls and activities at a local fair and the work people do there
misconceptions: Thinks only shopkeepers work at a mela
hooks: A village haat or the Pushkar mela

topics.title: Staying safe in a crowd
outcomes: Learner can say what to do if lost in a crowd and identify helpers like police
misconceptions: Believes it is safe to go with any stranger who offers help
hooks: Make a "lost child" plan: stay put, find a police uncle/aunty, say your parent’s phone number

topics.title: Festivals across India
outcomes: Learner can describe festivals celebrated in their region and others, and the food, flowers and seasons linked to them
misconceptions: Thinks everyone in India celebrates the same festivals in the same way
hooks: Bihu, Pongal, Baisakhi and Onam are all harvest festivals

topics.title: Signs and symbols around us
outcomes: Learner can read common signboards and symbols on the road
misconceptions: Believes signs are only for drivers
hooks: Zebra crossing and red-amber-green on the way to school

topics.title: Parts of a plant
outcomes: Learner can identify roots, stem, leaves, flowers and fruits in plants around them
misconceptions: Thinks all plants have flowers and fruits
Believes roots are always underground and never above
hooks: Banyan aerial roots; tulsi in the courtyard

topics.title: Herbs, shrubs, trees, climbers and creepers
outcomes: Learner can group plants by size and stem type and observe leaves by shape, smell and texture
misconceptions: Thinks grass is not a plant
hooks: Money plant climbing a wall; pumpkin creeping on the ground

topics.title: Plants as homes and food
outcomes: Learner can observe how insects, birds and small animals use plants for food and shelter
misconceptions: Believes a tree is just a tree and nothing lives in it
hooks: Count creatures on one neem tree for 10 minutes

topics.title: Animals in the soil
outcomes: Learner can describe tiny animals living in soil and leaf litter and how they help
misconceptions: Thinks earthworms are harmful pests
hooks: Look under a wet stone after rain

topics.title: Depending on each other
outcomes: Learner can give examples of how people, plants and animals depend on each other
misconceptions: Believes animals are only useful if they give us something
hooks: Bees, flowers and the honey in your kitchen

topics.title: Caring for plants and animals around us
outcomes: Learner can suggest safe ways to care for plants and animals in their surroundings
misconceptions: Believes feeding animals any human food is good for them
hooks: Water bowls for birds in summer; why not to feed monkeys chips at tourist spots

topics.title: Where our water comes from
outcomes: Learner can name sources of water (rain, wells, rivers, taps) and how it reaches homes
misconceptions: Thinks water just comes from the tap and never runs out
hooks: The journey of water to your home: well, handpump, tanker or pipe

topics.title: Storing and saving water
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to store water safely and avoid wasting it
misconceptions: Believes stored water is always clean
hooks: Catch rainwater from the roof; close the tap while brushing

topics.title: Food from plants and animals
outcomes: Learner can sort foods by source (plant, animal) and by how they are eaten (raw, cooked)
misconceptions: Thinks all food comes from shops
hooks: What is in your tiffin and where did it come from?

topics.title: Food in different seasons and places
outcomes: Learner can describe how food changes with seasons and regions
misconceptions: Believes everyone eats the same breakfast
hooks: Summer aam panna, winter sarson ka saag

topics.title: Healthy habits
outcomes: Learner can describe daily habits like brushing, bathing, sleeping and playing that keep us healthy
misconceptions: Thinks teeth only need brushing if they look dirty
hooks: Make a "my healthy day" chart

topics.title: Being safe at home and outside
outcomes: Learner can identify unsafe situations and ways to stay safe
misconceptions: Believes touching electric switches with wet hands is fine
hooks: Spot the dangers in a picture of a kitchen

topics.title: What things are made of
outcomes: Learner can group objects by material (wood, metal, glass, plastic, cloth) and describe their properties
misconceptions: Thinks all shiny things are metal
hooks: Find five things made of wood in your house

topics.title: See-through and opaque
outcomes: Learner can test which materials let light pass through
misconceptions: Believes only glass is transparent
hooks: Hold a polythene, paper and steel plate against a torch

topics.title: Things made by hand: pots and bricks
outcomes: Learner can describe how potters and brick makers shape clay and why it is baked
misconceptions: Thinks pots are made in factories only
hooks: Visit a kumhar’s wheel

topics.title: Patterns in handmade things
outcomes: Learner can observe and create patterns used in handmade objects
misconceptions: Believes handmade things are of lower quality
hooks: Patterns on a Madhubani painting or a pot

topics.title: Kinds of waste
outcomes: Learner can sort waste into wet and dry and say what can be reused
misconceptions: Thinks throwing waste in a dustbin makes it disappear
hooks: Green bin and blue bin at home

topics.title: Reduce, reuse, recycle
outcomes: Learner can suggest ways to reduce waste at home and school
misconceptions: Believes plastic rots like vegetable peels
hooks: Cloth bag for shopping; old bottles as planters
